subject: Operational findings and verification playbook — Dec 19 outage
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@orbitalpay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 21:03:00 -0800
Subject: Operational findings and verification playbook — Dec 19 outage

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for your patience this evening. We detected elevated error and truncated-response rates for requests routed to OrbitalPay between 20:42 and 20:58 PST on Dec 19. We triaged this as a customer-impacting inference service disruption and I want to share the immediate next steps:

- We're preparing a concise RCA and a customer verification playbook (attached) so your SREs can validate fixes end-to-end.
- We'll include a short timeline, owner list, and test scripts you can run against your integration.
- We'll propose a short joint verification window tomorrow (Dec 20) to run the playbook with your team.

High level: no credentials or raw customer data were exfiltrated. The impact manifested as an increased rate of incomplete streaming responses and higher latency for a subset of routed requests.

I'll send the draft RCA and the verification playbook in the next message. Can you confirm an available 30-minute slot between 10:00—13:00 PST tomorrow for a walk-through?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the update. Our SREs saw the same symptom (clients getting short/partial responses and a spike in reconnects). A couple quick clarifying questions before tomorrow:

1) Were any requests permanently dropped or replayed? We need to confirm idempotency concerns on our side.
2) Do you expect customer-facing tokens (session ids) were affected?

We can do 11:00 PST tomorrow for a 30-min call.

Subject: RE: Operational findings and verification playbook — Dec 19 outage

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming 11:00 PST. Below is the draft RCA and an abbreviated timeline plus the customer-facing verification steps we will walk through on the call. Attached: RCA-draft-20261220.pdf (full notes) and verification-playbook-OP.pdf (concise checklist).

Executive RCA summary (short):
- Root cause: During the evening traffic spike, a routing policy update that was deployed at 20:35 PST inadvertently matched a subset of OrbitalPay requests to a fallback model variant compiled with an incompatible KV cache layout. This caused key mismatches in the runtime cache layer, leading to repeated cache misses, longer kernel fallbacks, and truncated streaming outputs for about 3% of requests routed to your tenancy.
- Why it happened: a policy rule used an outdated feature flag name after a last-minute merge; our canary did not surface the mismatch on the short traffic pattern used in staging. The change interacted with kernel-selection heuristics on the serving runtime which expect compatible KV formats between model variants.
- Impact: increased 95th/99th percentile latency (+320ms median change for affected requests) and ~3% incomplete-response rate for OrbitalPay between 20:42 and 20:58 PST. No unauthorized data access was detected.

Concise timeline (local times):
- 20:24 PST — baseline traffic; first minor error spike (operations dashboard).
- 20:35 PST — routing policy change deployed to canary fleet (internal release tag: rwd-infer-3.4.12).
- 20:42 PST — error and truncated-response rate increases observed; automated routing fallback triggered for some requests.
- 20:48 PST — on-call engineers identified inconsistent KV cache behavior tied to model-variant selection.
- 20:53 PST — rollback of the policy rule across the active routing tier completed.
- 20:58 PST — metrics returned to baseline; post-recovery verification began.

Immediate customer action items (we will run these together at 11:00 PST):
1) Playbook step 1 — Controlled verification: run quick smoke curl/SDK checks defined in verification-playbook-OP.pdf to ensure your production tokenization and streaming paths observe full responses. Owner: OrbitalPay (SRE) with Redwood guidance.
2) Playbook step 2 — Log check: match request_ids from your logs to our timestamped-logs (attached) to confirm no duplicates or replays. Owner: OrbitalPay + Redwood engineering.
3) Playbook step 3 — End-to-end sample: replay 10 representative requests through your integration during the joint window to validate end-to-end integrity. Owner: Joint.

Corrective actions from Redwood (owner / ETA):
- Fix: revert the policy naming mismatch permanently and add unit checks for flag names in the router config pipeline. Owner: Runtime Config Team (Hannah Schmitt). ETA: 2026-12-21 EOD.
- Fix: add a runtime guard that verifies KV cache format compatibility at route selection time; fail closed to the preferred variant if incompatible. Owner: Serving Runtime Team (Marissa Cole). ETA: 2027-01-05.
- Prevent / Monitoring: add a canary traffic test that exercises the kernel-selection path used by your workload. Owner: Reliability Engineering. ETA: 2026-12-28.

Compensation/credits: we will propose a small service credit for the window of impact; details in the call and followed by a formal review.

Next steps for the call (11:00 PST):
- 5m — quick recap and roles
- 15m — run the verification playbook steps 1–3 together
- 10m — agree sign-off criteria and timeline for post-call action owners

If you'd like the RCA in a different format or need immediate copies of logs, please let me know; the timestamped logs are attached.

Regards,
Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Operational findings and verification playbook — Dec 19 outage

Thanks everyone for joining the verification window this morning. Quick notes and confirmation of next steps:

- Verification status: OrbitalPay ran the three playbook checks against production traffic during the joint window. All sampled requests returned full streaming responses and no duplicate/replayed request IDs were observed.
- RCA status: the draft RCA attached above reflects current findings; we will finalize the document after the follow-up internal test on Dec 21.
- Immediate commitments:
  * Hannah will deliver the config-name unit checks and a PR to the router pipeline (target: 2026-12-21 EOD).
  * Marissa will push the runtime guard with a feature flag off by default for staged rollout (target: 2027-01-05).
  * I will follow up with a formal credit proposal within 48 hours and share the final RCA.

Action items (owners and dates):
- OrbitalPay: confirm post-verification acceptance via email by EOD Dec 22. (Owner: Liam)
- Redwood: deliver final RCA and credit proposal by Dec 22. (Owner: Karthik)
- Redwood: implement config name unit tests and provide PR link. (Owner: Hannah)
- Redwood: staged runtime guard rollout plan and test plan. (Owner: Marissa)

Related links: Doc for verification playbook: https://redwood-docs.example.com/drive/OP-RCA-20261220, JIRA: JIRA-IMPACT-8792, HubSpot: HS-7643.

If you need a meeting note or to escalate to procurement/legal for the credit mechanics, I'll loop in the appropriate teams.

Appreciate the partnership — we'll keep you updated and circulate the final RCA.

Best,
Karthik
